message.content: The lion (Panthera leo) and the zebra (Equus quagga) share a common ancestor that is the last common ancestor of the entire Laurasiatheria clade. Laurasiatheria is a major group of placental mammals that includes carnivores (like lions), perissodactyls (like zebras), artiodactyls, cetaceans, bats, and a few other orders. This ancestor lived roughly 90 million years ago, after the divergence of the major placental mammal lineages but before the split between carnivores and perissodactyls.
